## Your job: question the recommendation {#d3s3-goal .reader-slide .s1-review .d3s3-review}

<div class="d9-goal"><strong>Before approving national expansion, ask the evaluator for evidence that could change your advice.</strong></div>

<div class="d9-three"><div><b>1</b><span>Find the claim and its source</span></div><div><b>2</b><span>Ask for a specific check</span></div><div><b>3</b><span>Make a conditional decision</span></div></div>

**Output:** two priority questions, an answer log and a short recommendation on H9 pages 2–5.

::: {.notes}
**5 minutes. Main point:** this is practice in commissioning and using evidence, not a new lesson on four evaluation designs. Give H9 pages 1–5; hold the separate E1–E8 evidence pack. Day 4 asks learners to audit a full report independently. Today they can ask an analyst questions. The core script totals 120 minutes; the Copilot extension is separate and optional.
:::

## The director wants a signature {#d3s3-note .reader-slide .s1-review .d3s3-review}

Read **H9-A on page 1**. Its three claims say the pilot clears the saving rule, four methods confirm success, and a benefit–cost ratio supports expansion.

<div class="d9-claims"><div><b>N1</b><span>Pilot saving: 1,014 AED. Minimum rule: 1,000 AED.</span></div><div><b>N2</b><span>Pilot and three city methods point to savings.</span></div><div><b>N3</b><span>RCT-linked modelled ratio: 2.44.</span></div></div>

::: {.ask}
On **page 3**, choose: sign, sign with conditions, or request evidence. Cite N1, N2, N3 or T9. What would you need to know before a national commitment?
:::

::: {.notes}
**8 minutes.** Allow four minutes of silent reading and writing before anyone speaks. H9-A is a deliberately contestable decision note, separate from tomorrow's report. The slide labels are shortened; participants must read the actual wording and Table T9. Record an individual opening reason, not a group vote. Do not reveal the weak claims yet. Transition: how far can each source speak?
:::

## One district is not the nation {#d3s3-reach .reader-slide .s1-review .d3s3-review}

<div class="d9-reach"><div><span class="d9-tag">Pilot RCT</span><b>400 businesses</b><small>One district; 200 assigned support, 200 comparison</small></div><span class="d9-arrow">→</span><div><span class="d9-tag">City analyses</span><b>10,000 records</b><small>Different city comparisons; 4,794 participants</small></div><span class="d9-arrow">→</span><div><span class="d9-tag">Proposed decision</span><b>National expansion</b><small>Target businesses and delivery conditions not established</small></div></div>

::: {.ask}
Which arrow needs evidence before the director treats a pilot result as a national forecast?
:::

::: {.notes}
**10 minutes. Main point:** a credible effect in the pilot district does not establish the effect under national delivery. Ask pairs what might differ: eligible businesses, take-up, implementers, costs or waste systems. H9-B on page 2 maps the comparisons. The city file is synthetic teaching data; no national transfer analysis is supplied. The city analyses do not automatically bridge the pilot-to-national gap. A bounded next phase remains an option.
:::

## Four methods; two sources of data {#d3s3-overlap .reader-slide .s1-review .d3s3-review}

<div class="d9-data-line"><div class="d9-source"><b>Separate pilot sample</b><span>Lottery comparison</span></div><div class="d9-source"><b>One city file</b><span>Difference in differences · score cut-off · matching</span></div></div>

<p class="d9-callout">The city methods reuse records and ask different comparison questions. Agreement in direction is useful; it is not four independent replications of a national effect.</p>

::: {.ask}
How would you rewrite N2 without counting the city analyses as separate votes?
:::

::: {.notes}
**7 minutes.** Give two minutes for a pair rewrite, then compare one cautious sentence. Accept: the pilot and three city analyses estimate lower annual waste costs in their respective comparisons; city analyses share records, target different groups and have different assumptions. This is retrieval from Days 1–2, not a rapid new lesson on each design. H9-B provides a reminder.
:::

## A positive effect can miss a minimum rule {#d3s3-threshold .reader-slide .s1-review .d3s3-review}

```{r, results='asis'}
html_out(d9_threshold_plot())
```

<div class="d9-twofacts"><span><b>Evidence of a reduction:</b> interval above zero</span><span><b>Minimum of 1,000 AED:</b> interval crosses the rule</span></div>

::: {.ask}
The point estimate is 1,014 AED. Can the note say the 1,000 AED minimum is settled?
:::

::: {.notes}
**10 minutes.** Ask for a prediction before tracing the interval. On a positive-saving scale, the pilot point estimate is about 1,014 AED per business per year at 12 months; its 95% interval is 862–1,167 AED. It lies above zero but spans the separate policy rule. A 95% interval is not a probability statement about a fixed effect; crossing a rule does not dictate risk tolerance. Day 3 Session 1 already calculated this result. Ask what evidence or risk tolerance could change the action.
:::

## A ratio is an argument with assumptions {#d3s3-economics .reader-slide .s1-review .d3s3-review}

<div class="d9-model"><div><span>RCT estimate</span><b>1,014 AED</b><small>Annual waste-cost saving at 12 months</small></div><div><span>Assumed delivery cost</span><b>1,800 AED</b><small>Per business at year 0</small></div><div><span>Assumed future</span><b>Years 1–5</b><small>Same saving each year; 5% rate</small></div><div class="d9-output"><span>Model result</span><b>2.44</b><small>Benefit–cost ratio under these inputs</small></div></div>

::: {.ask}
What actual cost or persistence evidence would you request before treating this as national value for money?
:::

::: {.notes}
**8 minutes.** Retrieve Session 1; do not recalculate. The RCT measured a 12-month cost outcome. Delivery cost, five equal saving years and rate are model inputs. The 2.44 ratio is a partial RCT-linked model, not a measured national return or complete appraisal. Invite requests about full incremental costs and persistence/transfer. The separate 1.86 city-study model appears in later materials; do not mix it into this clinic.
:::

## Turn a concern into an answerable request {#d3s3-question .reader-slide .s1-review .d3s3-review}

<p class="d9-weak">“Is the evaluation robust?”</p>

<div class="d9-request"><div><b>Claim</b><span>The pilot saving will apply nationally.</span></div><div><b>Evidence to send</b><span>Compare pilot and national businesses, delivery and follow-up.</span></div><div><b>Decision consequence</b><span>If they differ materially, test a bounded next phase first.</span></div></div>

::: {.ask}
Improve a question about N1, N2 or N3. Would the analyst know what to send?
:::

::: {.notes}
**9 minutes.** Give two minutes alone, three in pairs, four to hear examples. Model the difference between a judgement word and a document/result request. A useful question names the claim, needed evidence and how different answers affect action. Earlier trends could challenge city DiD; a score audit could address sorting; accounts could test cost. Do not imply missing checks exist. H9-B offers five families; groups will choose two priorities.
:::

## Two questions worth the analyst's time {#d3s3-prepare .reader-slide .s1-review .d3s3-review}

On **H9 page 3**, agree two requests. For each, write:

<div class="d9-three"><div><b>1</b><span>Evidence or document</span></div><div><b>2</b><span>What it tests</span></div><div><b>3</b><span>If/then action</span></div></div>

Rank them. Choose a spokesperson and a listener who will check the answer.

::: {.ask}
Which answer has the greatest chance of changing your recommendation?
:::

::: {.notes}
**8 minutes.** Two minutes alone, four to agree two questions, two to rank and assign roles. Eight groups may have different priorities. Avoid two near-identical requests and yes/no reassurance. Questions may target comparison, threshold, national reach, data quality or economics. Check that each could lead to a different action. The listener records the actual answer and source ID.
:::

## The analyst can say “not supplied” {#d3s3-role .reader-slide .s1-review .d3s3-review}

<div class="d9-clinic-rule"><div><b>Ask</b><span>One priority question</span></div><div><b>Listen</b><span>Evidence and source ID E1–E8</span></div><div><b>Follow up</b><span>What is still missing?</span></div></div>

The trainer releases only relevant evidence. Missing records stay missing.

::: {.notes}
**5 minutes.** Switch roles and open the trainer-held pack. Keep E1–E8 out of participants' hands until the relevant question is asked. Answer briefly from supplied evidence, state its limit, then show or read the ID. The optional question bank is a reference after the activity, not a script first. If an audit is unavailable, say so; do not invent a clean or failed audit. Participants log two substantial exchanges on H9 page 4, including another group's question.
:::

## Analyst clinic: ask, listen, follow up {#d3s3-clinic .reader-slide .s1-review .d3s3-review}

<div class="d9-clinic-board"><div><strong>Question asked</strong><span>What evidence could change the decision?</span></div><div><strong>Answer and source</strong><span>What was actually supplied?</span></div><div><strong>Still missing</strong><span>Which uncertainty remains?</span></div><div><strong>Next action</strong><span>Proceed, limit, test or defer?</span></div></div>

**H9 page 4:** log two useful exchanges, including another group's question.

::: {.notes}
**30 minutes.** With eight groups, allow about three minutes each for a question, short answer and follow-up; use six minutes to revisit the biggest gap. Map requests to E1 pilot/reach, E2 shared city comparisons, E3 rule/interval, E4 earlier trends, E5 cut-off, E6 matching, E7 data quality, E8 economic inputs. Read only relevant supplied evidence and limits, then show the ID. Suggested follow-ups guide the trainer but are not automatic answers. Log two substantial exchanges, not eight hurried transcriptions. Afterwards distribute evidence pages 1–4 for verification; retain page 5.
:::

## Did the answer meet the request? {#d3s3-rating .reader-slide .s1-review .d3s3-review}

<div class="d9-ratings"><div><b>Supported</b><span>The source answers the specific question.</span></div><div><b>Partial</b><span>It addresses one part; a relevant gap remains.</span></div><div><b>Unanswered</b><span>The check is absent or the reply changes topic.</span></div></div>

::: {.ask}
On **page 4**, rate one actual answer. Cite its source, name the gap and say what you would do next.
:::

::: {.notes}
**10 minutes.** Three minutes alone, three in pairs, four for contrasting examples. Rate against the question actually asked, not whether GreenWaste looks promising. E3 supports a request for the pilot interval but only partly addresses national expansion. E7 honestly discloses that real fieldwork documentation is absent; that quality request remains unanswered. Recognise supported evidence as well. This links the clinic to action.
:::

## What would you tell the director now? {#d3s3-final .reader-slide .s1-review .d3s3-review}

On **H9 page 5**, write four sentences:

1. **Action:** sign, sign with conditions, or request evidence.
2. **Basis:** one source and what it establishes.
3. **Boundary:** what it cannot yet establish.
4. **Next step:** one request and how either answer changes the action.

<p class="d9-callout">Your choice may stay the same. Your reason should become more precise.</p>

::: {.notes}
**10 minutes.** Five minutes independent writing, three to compare with opening reasons, two to hear different defensible decisions. A bounded next phase with evaluation and cost monitoring is plausible; requesting more evidence is also plausible. Do not require one button. Assess source fit, named uncertainty and accountable next action. Collect the advice before offering the optional Copilot extension. Day 4 uses a separate report without analyst access. **Core session ends at 120 minutes.**
:::

## Optional: does Copilot ask useful questions? {#d3s3-ai1 .reader-slide .s1-review .d3s3-review .d9-optional}

**15-minute extension outside the core session.** Use the separate Copilot handout.

Read a prepared response mixing sound checks with unsupported assurance. Keep one useful sentence, correct two claims, and add one decision-changing request.

::: {.notes}
**Optional 8 minutes.** Use extension page 1 after collecting independent advice. The response was written for this exercise, not captured from a live model. Verify against H9-A/H9-B and E1–E8. The early paragraphs make useful points; the final paragraph overstates independent replication, national certainty and data reliability.
:::

## Optional: verify the revision {#d3s3-ai2 .reader-slide .s1-review .d3s3-review .d9-optional}

Use the better prompt on extension page 2. Check the answer against H9-A/H9-B and E1–E8.

<div class="d9-request"><div><b>Keep</b><span>One useful, sourced request</span></div><div><b>Challenge</b><span>One unsupported assertion</span></div><div><b>Decide</b><span>Would your advice change?</span></div></div>

::: {.notes}
**Optional 7 minutes.** Use Copilot if available and approved, with only fictional sources. Otherwise use the prepared paper response. Require a source ID for a useful revision and a remaining claim. A fluent model response is not new evidence. The extension is not required for the 120-minute core.
:::
